packageRules.description: Ollama bumps stay a manual call (model-pull history, task #25), but Renovate still tracks the tag: new versions are listed on the Dependency Dashboard and a PR is only created when its box is ticked there.

linuxserver.io tags are <app version>-ls<build> (v1.6.0-ls356, 2.5.2.5491-ls155, v26.2-ls256). Docker versioning reads -ls356 as a suffix that must match exactly, so it never offered a rebuild (where linuxserver ships base-image security fixes) and almost never an app bump. Here the ls build number is the last version component, so every newer build is offered. The version-* alias tags don't match and are ignored.

qBittorrent's linuxserver tags also carry the libtorrent version: 5.2.3_v2.0.13-ls469. The libtorrent major is the compatibility part, so it stays on libtorrent 2.x and never jumps to the libtorrentv1-* tags.

VectorChord tags are pg<postgres major>-v<extension version> (pg17-v0.4.1), which docker versioning can't parse. Stay on Postgres 17 and VectorChord 0.4.x: the extension API changed in 1.x and Streamystats' schema is written against 0.4 (see statefulset-vectorchord.yaml).

SearXNG tags are <date>-<commit> (2026.7.3-747cec4c2). Docker versioning reads the commit hash as a suffix that must match, so it never offered an update. Compare the date only. Upstream ships several builds a day, so only raise its PR early on Mondays.

Floating tags (major or major.minor only: alpine:3.24, busybox:1.38, mikefarah/yq:4, python:3.14-slim, postgres:18) are rebuilt in place upstream, so a security fix changes the image without changing the tag, and nodes keep running whatever they cached. Pinning the digest makes Renovate raise a PR whenever the image behind the tag changes.

Kea: ISC numbers stable releases with an even minor (2.6, 3.0, 3.2) and development releases with an odd one (2.7, 3.1, 3.3), so only offer even minors. dhcp4 and kea-admin (the init container that upgrades the database schema) must run the same version, so they update together in one PR.

ClickHouse (Langfuse's trace store): LTS releases only. ClickHouse's LTS lines are the .3 and .8 releases (26.3, 26.8, 27.3, ...), supported about a year; regular releases get about three months. Langfuse v4 needs >= 25.12.
kubectl is only supported within one minor version of the API server. The cluster runs Kubernetes 1.35 (Talos), so allow 1.35.x and 1.36.x. Widen this when Talos/Kubernetes is upgraded (task #33).

Hermes switched from CalVer tags (v2026.9.24) to SemVer (v0.22.5) in October 2026. Without this, Renovate treats the old CalVer tags as the biggest version and never offers SemVer releases, and it would also offer the -desktop and rc. tags. Only plain vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
Langfuse web and worker must run the same version, so they update together in one PR.
hermes-webui publishes several releases a day, and each update restarts Hermes for ~3 minutes. Only create/update its PR overnight (Adelaide), so there is at most one bump a day.
cilium and argocd are manual-sync: merging does nothing until someone syncs them, and a full sync is the risky part.
prBodyNotes: This app is manual-sync. After merging, review `argocd app diff` and sync deliberately; never full-sync cilium or argocd without checking the diff.
